claims.claim: Only the Azure Databricks catalog structure is mirrored and data is accessed through shortcuts, with no data movement; auto-sync of future catalog changes is on by default; propagation takes seconds to several minutes.
Unsupported table types: RLS/CLM tables, Lakehouse federated tables, Delta Sharing tables, streaming tables, views and materialized views; the Databricks ADLS account must be accessible to Fabric.
Unity Catalog permissions are not mirrored; the connection credential is used for all data queries; UC policies are not enforced at the storage layer.
Unity Catalog information_schema.tables reports table_type values including MANAGED, EXTERNAL, VIEW, MATERIALIZED_VIEW, STREAMING_TABLE and FOREIGN.

concept_html:
Your Track A pipelines write gold tables into Unity Catalog. Mirroring Azure Databricks Unity Catalog makes them readable in Fabric without copying them. Unlike database mirroring, no data moves. Fabric mirrors only the catalog structure (catalogs, schemas, tables) and reads the underlying Delta files through shortcuts.

You get a mirrored Azure Databricks item with a SQL analytics endpoint, and you can build Power BI reports on it in Direct Lake mode. By default, Automatically sync future catalog changes for the selected schema is on, so new tables appear. Propagation takes from seconds to several minutes.

Three rules decide whether it works and whether it is safe (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026):

1. Some table types do not mirror: tables with row filters or column masks (RLS/CLM policies), Lakehouse federated tables, Delta Sharing tables, streaming tables, views and materialized views. The ADLS Gen2 account behind the Databricks workspace must also be reachable from Fabric.

2. Unity Catalog permissions do not carry over. Grants on catalogs, schemas and tables in Databricks do not apply in Fabric. You rebuild access with Fabric's model: workspace roles, item permissions, SQL permissions, OneLake security.

3. One credential reads everything. The credential used to create the connection is used for all data queries. Unity Catalog policies such as row filters, column masks or ABAC are not enforced at the storage layer, so they would not apply to direct storage access anyway.

Put together: mirror tables that are safe to share at the level you grant in Fabric. For data that needs row-level rules, publish a gold table without the policy that already contains only what the audience may see, or apply the rules again in Fabric.

Return, sorted, the names that can be mirrored: table_type must be "MANAGED" or "EXTERNAL", and the table must not have a row filter or column mask. exercises.solution:
MIRRORABLE_TYPES = frozenset({"MANAGED", "EXTERNAL"})


def mirror_eligible(tables: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[str]:
    """Unity Catalog tables that Fabric can mirror.

    Args:
        tables: Dicts with name, table_type and has_row_filter_or_mask.

    Returns:
        Sorted names of eligible tables.
    """
    return sorted(
        str(t["name"])
        for t in tables
        if t["table_type"] in MIRRORABLE_TYPES and not t["has_row_filter_or_mask"]
    )

title: Mirroring Azure Databricks Unity Catalog into Fabric
why_html: A team mirrored their gold schema so that regional managers could build Power BI reports. In Databricks, a row filter limited each manager to their region (lesson A4-L3). The filtered table did not appear in Fabric at all, so the team created an unfiltered copy for the mirror, with a connection that could read every row. Every manager with Viewer access now saw every region. The rules had lived in Unity Catalog, and nothing had been rebuilt in Fabric.
